title: In situ Grain Growth Experiments: TEM Imaging & Automated Segmentation with Correlative 4D-STEM Orientation Mapping
content: Direct microstructure design is a grand challenge problem in materials engineering, but no prescriptive models successfully describe the dynamics of grain growth: microstructural design today relies on trial-and-error, and model development is bottlenecked by the availability of high quality time-series data. Grain growth is governed by the complex interactions among the ensemble of crystallites and their interfaces, i.e. grain boundaries (GBs), and thus can only be described in high parameter spaces. To fully characterize the phenomenon, one must account for the (1) geometric and topological features of the microstructure, including grain size distribution (GSD), grain side-class, GB curvature, and more; and (2) the bicrystallography of each GB, described macroscopically by a 5-parameter character (3 for misorientation, 2 for GB plane inclination) [1]. As a result, to adequately sample the space and draw meaningful conclusions about microstructure and its evolution requires enormous amounts of data and, critically, the infrastructure to interpret it. In this work, we leverage thin films’ columnar microstructure, as shown in Figure 1a, to demonstrate a multi-modal in situ scanning/transmission electron microscopy (S/TEM)-based approach for dynamic, complete, and nondestructive characterization of grain growth at scale.
